facts.statement: Eotriceratops was a herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in North America during the late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Eotriceratops (meaning "dawn three-horned face") is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaurs which lived in the area of North America during the late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The genus Eotriceratops was named and described by Xiao-Chun Wu, Donald B. Brinkman, David A. Eberth, and Dennis R. Braman in 2007.
facts.quote: Eotriceratops was named and described by Xiao-Chun Wu, Donald B. Brinkman, David A. Eberth and Dennis R. Braman in 2007.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown discovered the skeleton of Eotriceratops in August 1910 in southern Alberta, Canada, but neglected it at the time.
facts.quote: In early August 1910, Barnum Brown during an American Museum of Natural History expedition discovered a large dinosaur skeleton in the Dry Island site, on the west bank of the Red Deer River in southern Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: The species name xerinsularis means "of the dry island" and refers to the Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific name xerinsularis, means "of the dry island", from Greek ξηρός, xèros, "dry", and Latin insula, "island" and is a reference to the Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park where its remains were found.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen lived about 68.8 million years ago during the early Maastrichtian stage of the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, RTMP 2002.57.5, was found in a layer of the uppermost Horseshoe Canyon Formation, dated to the early Maastrichtian, about 68.8 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Eotriceratops was estimated to have been around 3 meters long.
facts.quote: The holotype skull has been estimated to have had an original length of around 3 m.

facts.statement: Eotriceratops was a large animal measuring between 8.5 and 9 meters in length with a body mass of 11 metric tons.
facts.quote: It would have been a large animal, measuring 8.5 - 9 m in length and 11 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The eye horns of Eotriceratops were forward-curving and estimated to be 80 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The horns above the eyes were forward-curving and have been estimated at 80 cm long.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows three bite marks above the eye interpreted as traces of scavenging behavior.
facts.quote: Three bite marks can be observed above the eye, near the base of the left horn, which were interpreted as traces of scavenging.

facts.statement: Eotriceratops is classified within the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Eotriceratops was in 2007 placed in the Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis suggests Eotriceratops was a close relative and sister species to Triceratops, Nedoceratops, and Torosaurus.
facts.quote: In a cladistic analysis, it was recovered as a close relative of Triceratops, Nedoceratops and Torosaurus. It would have been the sister species of Triceratops.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether Eotriceratops is the sister species of Triceratops or a more basal ancestor to it due to its greater age.
facts.quote: In view of its greater age, the describing authors considered it more likely that Eotriceratops was in fact basal to, lower in the evolutionary tree than, the other three genera.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul renamed the species Triceratops xerinsularis in 2010, but this classification is not widely accepted by other researchers.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul renamed the species Triceratops xerinsularis, but this inclusion of Eotriceratops in the existing genus Triceratops has not been followed by other researchers.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Eotriceratops bore at least thirty-five tooth positions.
facts.quote: The maxilla bore at least thirty-five tooth positions.

facts.statement: The squamosal bone of Eotriceratops shows at least five episquamosals.
facts.quote: The squamosal shows at least five episquamosals.

facts.statement: Eotriceratops had a skull estimated to be about 3 meters long with a short frill.
facts.quote: Se ha calculado que el cráneo tenía unos 3 metros de largo, con una gola corta.

facts.statement: Estimates for the total length of Eotriceratops range from 9 to 12 meters.
facts.quote: Esto ha llevado a estimaciones de su tamaño total de alrededor de los 12 metros, pero posteriores trabajos más conservadores lo sitúan en el rango de los 9 metros.

facts.statement: In 2010, Paul estimated Eotriceratops to be 8.5 meters long and weigh ten tonnes.
facts.quote: En 2010, Paul estimó su longitud en 8,5 metros, su peso en diez toneladas.

facts.statement: The eye horns of Eotriceratops curved forward and were estimated to be about 80 centimeters long.
facts.quote: Los cuernos sobre los ojos estaban curvados hacia adelante y se han estimado en unos 80 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Three bite marks were found on the eye area near the base of the left horn, interpreted as evidence of scavenging behavior.
facts.quote: Se pueden observar tres marcas de mordedura sobre el ojo, cerca de la base del cuerno izquierdo, que se interpretaron como rastros de carroñeo.

facts.statement: The squamosal bone of Eotriceratops shows at least five epoccipitals.
facts.quote: El escamoso muestra al menos cinco epoccipitales.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown discovered a large dinosaur skeleton at Dry Island in southern Alberta, Canada, in early August 1910.
facts.quote: A principios de agosto de 1910, Barnum Brown, durante una expedición del Museo Americano de Historia Naturall, descubrió un gran esqueleto de dinosaurio en el sitio de Dry Island, en la orilla oeste del río Red Deer en el sur de Alberta, Canadá.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen RTMP 2002.57.5 dates to the early Maastrichtian, approximately 67.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, RTMP 2002.57.5, se ha encontrado en una de las capas más alta de la Formación de cañón de herradura, que data de los pprincipios del Maastrichtiano, hace aproximadamente 67,6 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton with a skull but lacks the lower jaws.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial con cráneo, que carece de las mandíbulas inferiores.

facts.statement: Eotriceratops was placed in the subfamily Chasmosaurinae in 2007.
facts.quote: Eotriceratops se colocó en 2007 en la subfamilia Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis recovered Eotriceratops as a close relative of Triceratops, Nedoceratops, and Torosaurus, making it a sister species to Triceratops.
facts.quote: En un análisis cladístico, se recuperó como un pariente cercano de Triceratops , Nedoceratops y Torosaurus, que son todos de los últimos depósitos de Maastrichtiense,por lo que habría sido una especie hermana de Triceratops.

facts.statement: Due to its older age, the authors considered Eotriceratops to be more basal, or lower on the evolutionary tree, than Triceratops, Nedoceratops, and Torosaurus.
facts.quote: En vista de su mayor edad, los autores que lo describieron consideraron que era más probable que Eotriceratops fuera en realidad basal, más bajo en el árbol evolutivo que los otros tres géneros.

facts.statement: The ceratopsid specimen was found between coal seams and dates to 67.6–68 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen del ceratópsido fue recogido entre las costuras del carbón y tiene una edad de 67,6-68 millones de años.

facts.statement: Eotriceratops is older than any other Triceratops-group ceratopsid, filling a biostratigraphic gap between early and late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Así, Eotriceratops es más viejo que cualquier otro ceratópsido del grupo del Triceratops, y el descubrimiento del E. xerinsularis llena un espacio bioestratigrafico entre el Mastrichtiano temprano y tardío.

facts.statement: Eotriceratops belongs to the tribe Triceratopsini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Triceratopsini

facts.statement: Eotriceratops is classified in the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Eotriceratops is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Eotriceratops lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul renamed the species Triceratops xerinsularis, but this change was not adopted by other researchers.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul cambió el nombre de la especie a Triceratops xerinsularis, pero esto no fue seguido por otros investigadores.

facts.statement: Eotriceratops is very similar to Triceratops but is 2 million years older, more primitive, and also large in size.
facts.quote: Es muy parecido al famoso Triceratops, aunque 2 millones de años más antiguo, más primitivo y también de gran tamaño.

rejected.quote: The expedition's cook, Glen Guthrie, rediscovered the skeleton by accident.
